age.evidence: Adult male C57BL/6J mice (8 weeks old) were purchased from Envigo

sex.evidence: Adult male C57BL/6J mice (8 weeks old)

dosing.evidence: Two doses of psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline (5 mL/kg, i.p.) were administered on the last two weeks of the stress protocol: week 5 (day 29) and week 6 (day 36)

day_night_flipped.evidence: housed under standard laboratory conditions on a 12 h light/dark cycle (direction not specified)

assays.assay_description: Mice placed in open field arena (43 × 43 × 43 cm, 60 lux) immediately after psilocybin/saline i.p. injection and recorded for 25 min; HTR manually counted for last 20 min. Tested on day 29 (first dose) and day 36 (second dose).

application_type.evidence: Two doses of psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.)

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were placed in an open field arena

food_restriction.evidence: no food in HTR arena during recording

water_restriction.evidence: no water in HTR arena during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately following psilocybin/saline administration, animals were placed in an open field arena

sample_size.evidence: The HTR was measured in psilocybin-treated animals (n = 16). However, since saline-treated mice exhibited an HTR close to zero in every single animal, only a subgroup of animals (n = 8) was required for the control-saline and CUMS-saline groups evaluation

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin robustly induced HTR in both control and CUMS mice. The second administration produced significantly more head-twitches than the first in both groups, indicating sensitization.
outcomes.evidence: The control group exhibited a higher number of head-twitches on the second administration (t = 3.107, p <0.01). Likewise, higher HTR was observed in the CUMS animals on the second psilocybin administration (t = 5.753, p <0.0001)

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is a drug-induced response, not ethological

B7_automated_classification.evidence: A trained and blinded observer manually quantified the HTR

D1_continuity.evidence: First dose day 29 and second dose day 36 both recorded

assays.assay_description: Two-bottle choice (2% sucrose vs water) in home cage following 8-h fast; bottles available for 15 h. Tested at baseline (day -2), week 4 (day 26) and week 6 (day 38).

setup_habituation.evidence: Previous to the beginning of the stress protocol, a training phase was performed for 48 h

food_restriction.evidence: An 8-h fasting period was set to promote water/sucrose (2%) consumption

time_to_assay.evidence: week 6 (day 38, after psilocybin administration); last dose day 36

sample_size.evidence: n = 16 per group for behavioural evaluation

outcomes.summary: CUMS reduced sucrose preference at week 4 (anhedonia). Psilocybin restored preference in CUMS mice at week 6.
outcomes.statistics: Week 4: t=3.80, p<0.001. Week 6: Fi(1,47)=9.923, p<0.01; control-saline vs CUMS-saline t=3.373, p<0.01; CUMS-saline vs CUMS-psilocybin t=2.316, p<0.05.
outcomes.evidence: CUMS-psilocybin animals showed increased preference, compared to their saline-treated counterparts. Two-way ANOVA showed significant interaction between factors (Fi(1,47) = 9.923, p < 0.01)

E8_food_water.evidence: Bottles were placed in cages at 17:00, and left for 15 h

D2_session_duration.evidence: left for 15 h — but recording was the integrated 15-h consumption period; >6 h technically

D5_followup.evidence: week 6 (day 38, after psilocybin administration) — 2 days after last dose

D6_circadian.evidence: bottles left for 15 h (>6 h continuous)

assays.assay_description: Standard EPM on day 43. Time in open arms, percentage of entries to open arms, time in closed arms and latency to closed arms scored from video by blinded researcher.

time_to_assay.evidence: EPM testing was performed on day 43; last dose day 36

sample_size.evidence: n = 16 per group for behavioural evaluation

outcomes.summary: CUMS reduced open-arm entries and increased closed-arm time. Psilocybin did not significantly affect EPM measures in individual analyses.
outcomes.statistics: % entries open: FCUMS(1,57)=6.501, p<0.05. Time in closed: FCUMS(1,57)=14.910, p<0.001. Latency to closed: FCUMS(1,55)=9.37, p<0.01; FPsil(1,55)=1.79, ns.
outcomes.evidence: No significant effect of psilocybin or interaction between factors was found

B1_num_measures.evidence: time in open arms, percentage of entries, time in closed arms, latency to closed arms

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manual video scoring by blinded researcher

E2_shelter.evidence: closed arms not counted as shelter per rubric

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM not counted as multiple compartments per rubric

D1_continuity.evidence: EPM testing was performed on day 43

D2_session_duration.evidence: duration not explicitly stated; standard EPM <15 min, but value not reported

assays.assay_description: Day 44: each mouse in individual cage with one square of nesting material; nest quality scored on 1–5 scale after 30 min.

food_restriction.evidence: home-cage testing with ad libitum food

water_restriction.evidence: home-cage testing with ad libitum water

time_to_assay.evidence: NBT on day 44; last dose day 36

sample_size.evidence: n = 16 per group for behavioural evaluation

outcomes.summary: CUMS caused deficits in nest-building. Psilocybin did not rescue these deficits.
outcomes.statistics: Kruskal-Wallis=47.71, p<0.0001; control-saline vs CUMS-saline Z=4.64, p<0.0001; CUMS-saline vs CUMS-psilocybin Z=0.76, ns.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin did not rescue such deficits (CUMS-saline vs CUMS-psilocybin, Z = 0.76, p >0.05)

B4_ethological.evidence: nest-building is a natural ethological behaviour

E1_environment_type.evidence: Each mouse was kept in individual cages

E4_nesting.evidence: One square of nesting material was introduced in each cage

E8_food_water.evidence: home cage with ad libitum food/water

D2_session_duration.evidence: Nest-building skills were evaluated 30 min later

assays.assay_description: Day 45: mice placed in centre of arena and allowed to explore for 10 min; total distance and time in centre tracked with Smart 3.0.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were carefully placed in the centre of the arena and left to explore

time_to_assay.evidence: OFT on day 45; last dose day 36

sample_size.evidence: n = 16 per group for behavioural evaluation

outcomes.summary: CUMS and psilocybin independently increased total distance travelled; time in centre was reduced in CUMS groups regardless of treatment.
outcomes.evidence: The CUMS protocol induced increased exploratory activity in the OFT, as well as psilocybin did

B1_num_measures.evidence: total distance and time in centre

assays.assay_description: Day 46: 16-h food deprivation, open field arena filled with sawdust and single pellet in centre illuminated (800–900 lux); latency to chew/bite pellet recorded (max 10 min).

food_restriction.evidence: Food pellets were removed from cage grids 16 h prior to the NSFT

time_to_assay.evidence: NSFT on day 46; last dose day 36

sample_size.evidence: n = 16 per group for behavioural evaluation

outcomes.summary: CUMS increased latency to feed; psilocybin did not rescue this increase.
outcomes.evidence: An increased latency to feed in the NSFT was observed in CUMS groups, and psilocybin did not rescue such increase

E3_bedding.evidence: An open field arena was filled with sawdust

E8_food_water.evidence: single pellet attached to the ground was placed in the centre

D2_session_duration.evidence: A period of 10 min was set as the maximum latency time permitted

assays.assay_description: Day 47: mice suspended by tail for 6 min; immobility time manually scored.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were hung from a piece of tape stuck to the tail

time_to_assay.evidence: TST on day 47; last dose day 36

sample_size.evidence: n = 16 per group for behavioural evaluation

outcomes.summary: CUMS increased immobility; psilocybin rescued the immobility increase in CUMS mice.
outcomes.statistics: FPsil(1,46)=9.907, p<0.01; Fi(1,46)=9.045, p<0.01; control-saline vs CUMS-saline t=3.207, p<0.01; CUMS-saline vs CUMS-psilocybin t=3.965, p<0.001
outcomes.evidence: The CUMS-saline group showed increased immobility-time in the TST. This effect was rescued by treatment in the CUMS group

D2_session_duration.evidence: The duration of the test was 6 min

assays.assay_description: Day 48: modified Porsolt swim test in cylinders (24 cm height × 20 cm diameter, 18 cm water at 24°C) for 6 min; immobility, swimming and climbing scored during last 4 min.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice placed in water-filled cylinders, unable to escape (FST cylinder per rubric)

water_restriction.evidence: water present as test medium, not drinkable

time_to_assay.evidence: FST on day 48; last dose day 36

sample_size.evidence: n = 16 per group for behavioural evaluation

outcomes.summary: CUMS increased immobility and decreased swimming/climbing. Psilocybin reduced immobility and restored swimming in CUMS mice but did not affect climbing.
outcomes.evidence: Increased immobility-time induced by CUMS was observed in the FST. Psilocybin rescued such effect in stressed mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: The mobility (swimming and climbing behaviours) and the immobility were quantified

B4_ethological.evidence: FST behaviours not ethological per rubric

E1_environment_type.evidence: Four cylinders (24 cm height × 20 cm diameter)

judge_notes: Dropped the 'Coat state assessment' that only qwen included — this is a physical/physiological observation of fur condition, not a behavioural recording session, and is better classified as descriptive metadata.

Merged candidates' HTR entries into one assay. Scored D1=1 (multiple discrete sessions on day 29 and 36) per glm/gptoss reasoning, since both dosing days produced reported HTR data; same paradigm repeated = 1 assay per rubric.

Sucrose preference D2 set to 2 (61 min–6 h) reflecting 15-h bottle access — strictly >6 h falls in '>6 h' category per the rubric cutoffs, so revised D2=2 and D6=1 (>=6 h continuous). On reflection, 15 h does exceed 6 h, so kept D6=1 (circadian) consistent with glm.
EPM E2 scored 0 per rubric: closed arms are part of apparatus design, not a shelter (overrode glm's score of 1).

NBT scored as home cage (E1=1) with bedding (E3=1) and nesting (E4=1) — home cage standard bedding is typically present; conservative E8=1 reflects ad libitum food/water in home cage during the 30-min test.
FST setup_restrain scored 'yes' per rubric explicit example (FST cylinder = restraint).
Coat state was excluded as not a behavioural recording session per task rules.
